_comment: Worked example: register a LOCAL DEV GitHub OAuth app in the web console and capture its client id/secret.
Built from a real hand-driven agent-browser session (comet profile, CDP 127.0.0.1:9222, --session comet).
Keys starting with '_' are ignored by pixel (not part of the Flow schema); they are documentation for humans.
HOW TO RUN
pixel flow save github-oauth-app --from-file crates/pixel-flow/examples/github-oauth-app.json
pixel flow run github-oauth-app [--var app_name='My Local Dev App'] [--var callback_url=http://localhost:3000/oauth/github/callback]
OAUTH_ENV_OUT=./.env.oauth crates/pixel-flow/examples/oauth-env.py capture github
OAUTH_ENV_OUT=./.env.oauth crates/pixel-flow/examples/oauth-env.py check github
WHY THE LAST TWO COMMANDS ARE NOT FLOW STEPS
pixel-flow can click/fill/type/press/wait/scroll/eval, but `eval` output is discarded by `pixel flow run`, and a flow
cannot write files, read env vars or call curl. So the flow drives the browser until the one-time secret is ON SCREEN,
then oauth-env.py reads it straight from the page into $OAUTH_ENV_OUT (mode 600) and prints only lengths. Nothing
secret passes through the flow log, the agent transcript, or argv.
LOGIN IS OUT OF SCOPE. The comet session must already be signed in to GitHub. If a login or sudo-mode page shows up the
flow STOPS on purpose (a `click` whose ref_hint can never match; the engine aborts with that text as the error). It never
types credentials. Sign in by hand in Comet, then re-run.
NOT IDEMPOTENT: every run registers a NEW app. Delete stale local-dev apps by hand in the console.
No terms-of-service checkbox exists on this form, so there is no accept_terms var here (the Atlassian and Notion flows have one).
AFTER THE FLOW (manual follow-up): your backend/app reads OAUTH_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID / OAUTH_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET from its
process environment. `source` the env file written to $OAUTH_ENV_OUT before starting the API. Never commit that file.
NEVER put real client ids or secrets in this file.
name: github-oauth-app
title: Register a local-dev GitHub OAuth app and capture client id/secret
description: Registers a local-dev GitHub OAuth app (default name 'My Local Dev App') at github.com/settings/applications/new with non-expiring user tokens, generates a client secret, and stops with the one-time secret visible on screen. Follow with `oauth-env.py capture github` to write OAUTH_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID / OAUTH_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET to $OAUTH_ENV_OUT (mode 600), then `oauth-env.py check github`. Login is out of scope; the flow stops if signed out. Not idempotent.
preconditions: Verify comet-cdp is up (port 9222) and `agent-browser --session comet tab list` answers
The comet browser profile is ALREADY signed in to github.com (this flow never types credentials)
Export OAUTH_ENV_OUT=<path> before the capture step (the file receives secrets: keep it out of git, mode 600 is enforced)

vars.name: app_name
vars.description: Application name shown on GitHub's consent screen

vars.name: homepage_url
vars.description: Homepage URL of the local app

vars.name: callback_url
vars.description: Redirect URI your local app's OAuth callback route listens on

steps.rationale: Open the new-OAuth-app form. Already-authenticated profile expected; GitHub redirects to /login when signed out.
steps.on_failure: If the open times out, re-run `agent-browser --session comet tab list` and retry once

steps.rationale: Let the form (or a login redirect) finish rendering before the signed-in check
Login is out of scope. Signed-out sessions land on the sign-in form; stop instead of touching credentials.
steps.condition: page shows 'Username or email address' or 'Sign in to GitHub'

then.rationale: STOP: not signed in to GitHub in the comet session. Sign in by hand in Comet, then re-run this flow. (This step fails on purpose; its ref_hint can never match, so the flow aborts with this message.)
then.ref_hint: STOP - GitHub login required in the comet session - a human must sign in, then re-run the flow

steps.rationale: Capture the form: textboxes Application name, Homepage URL, Application description, Redirect URI
Application name (shown to users on the consent screen)
Redirect URI = the backend callback. Must match exactly, including scheme and port.

PITFALL: 'Expire user access tokens' is checked by default and token handling that assumes NON-expiring gho_ tokens, so it must be UNCHECKED. Idempotent: clicks only when currently checked. Wrapped in an IIFE because the page context keeps top-level const/let between evals, so a second eval declaring the same name would throw.
steps.on_failure: If the checkbox is not found, re-snapshot and click the checkbox labelled 'Expire user access tokens' ONLY if it is checked. Do not submit with it checked.

steps.rationale: Verify the filled values and that 'Expire user access tokens' is now unchecked before submitting (the registration is not undoable except by deleting the app)
Submit the form. GitHub redirects to https://github.com/settings/applications/<id>.
PITFALL: the redirect to the app page can lag the click; give it time before looking for the secret button
Confirm we are on the new app's settings page (URL /settings/applications/<id>), not still on /new with a validation error
Generate the client secret. GitHub shows it ONCE; the next step must not reload or navigate away.
steps.ref_hint: button containing 'Generate a new client secret'
steps.on_failure: If the button is missing the app page may not have loaded; wait 2s, re-snapshot, retry. Never click twice: each click mints another secret.

steps.rationale: Let the secret render. A sudo-mode 'Confirm access' page may appear instead (handled by the next step).
GitHub sudo mode asks to re-verify the account before minting a secret. That is a credential prompt: stop and ask the human.
steps.condition: page shows 'Confirm access' or 'Verify it' or 'Use your passkey'

then.rationale: STOP: GitHub is asking to re-verify the account (sudo mode). A human must confirm in Comet, then click 'Generate a new client secret' by hand (do not re-run the whole flow: that would register a second app).
then.ref_hint: STOP - GitHub sudo-mode confirmation required - a human must confirm in Comet before the secret is generated

steps.rationale: FLOW ENDS HERE with the one-time secret visible on the page (client id = 20 alphanumerics after the 'Client ID' label; secret = first 40-hex string in the page HTML). DO NOT RELOAD. NEXT: OAUTH_ENV_OUT=<path> crates/pixel-flow/examples/oauth-env.py capture github   then   ... check github

success_signal: page text contains 'Client ID' and 'Client secrets'. Then run: OAUTH_ENV_OUT=<path> oauth-env.py capture github && oauth-env.py check github (a 404 from GitHub means the credentials are valid, 401 means invalid)
